relational_session_contract.state_relation: every State occurrence is the same concrete closed ordinary type

phases.open: None plus open -> accept or reject
phases.active: Some(State) plus message or tick -> continue or close
phases.terminal: Some(State) plus peer_close or shutdown -> finish

relational_session_contract.independent_oracle: src/platform/session.rs reconstructs the relation through a disjoint SessionShapeRead implementation and rejects mismatched repeated state or live retained stream state
relational_session_contract.transition_commit: one callback at a time; reserve configured maximum output first; validate complete next state and output; commit the whole batch; then install state
relational_session_contract.failure: failure, cancellation, exhaustion, malformed output, or a phase-invalid decision installs neither next state nor partial output, ends admission, cancels and joins children, closes streams, drops queued state/output, and releases permits once
relational_session_contract.effects: already performed effects retain the existing possible-visibility contract and are never replayed

negative_boundaries: truncated, corrupt, symlinked, non-regular, and foreign artifacts

runtime_and_bounds.ownership: one resident parent session scope owns the upgraded connection, reader, ordered driver, writer, coalesced tick, cancellation lineage, child joins, retained ordinary state, task stream leases, permits, and byte-accounted mailboxes; children cannot detach
runtime_and_bounds.callback: each transition is a finite resident task with its own deadline, work, and resource scope; the maintained descriptor uses a 30-second callback deadline while session lifetime is independently 24 hours
runtime_and_bounds.transport_event_order: completed application messages and one coalesced tick enter one ordered driver; a tick never overtakes an accepted transport event and at most one tick is pending
runtime_and_bounds.backpressure: the writer reserves one maximum transition batch before a potentially effectful callback, so a slow writer prevents a later callback rather than exposing an effect followed only by queue failure
runtime_and_bounds.cleanup: overload rejects before upgrade; failure or shutdown stops callbacks, cancels siblings, joins children, closes task streams, drops state and queued messages, attempts one bounded close where valid, and returns active/pending counters to zero

maintained_lkjournal.authority: the graph owns /live selection, bearer-session validation, strict JSON-array grammar, subscription transition state, actor filtering, data scans, revision detection, deterministic ordering, message construction, errors, and close decisions
maintained_lkjournal.host_exclusions: Rust owns no lkjournal route, token rule, JSON operation parser, subscription map, scan/filter/order rule, sequence or revision cursor, message shape, or actor policy
behavior: two raw clients authenticated as one actor retain independent subscription maps
subscribe or replace emits the current deterministic actor-owned snapshot and end marker
HTTP create at revision 0 and update at revision 1 are pushed after graph ticks
replacement and unsubscribe on one connection do not affect the other
a second actor observes none of the first actor's resources
an unread subscribed client does not block ping/pong on another admitted client
restart drops connection state but preserves durable data; reconnect and resubscribe reconstruct revision 1

rfc6455_and_raw_oracle.server: plaintext RFC 6455 over the existing HTTP/1.1 listener; no extension or subprotocol negotiation
rfc6455_and_raw_oracle.codec: one production path supplied by the enabled locked Axum/Tokio/Tungstenite graph
rfc6455_and_raw_oracle.graph_boundary: graph sees normalized open metadata, completed text/binary message identity with a task-scoped byte stream, coalesced ticks, validated peer close, and shutdown; it never sees frames, masking, fragmentation, ping, or pong
rfc6455_and_raw_oracle.raw_client: tools/lkjscript-dev/src/raw_websocket.rs independently implements bounded TCP HTTP upgrade, SHA-1, Base64, client masking, server frame decoding, fragmentation, ping/pong, close, and malformed cases without importing production WebSocket helpers
